suggestions.assertion: A draft .md file is written to 04-gmb/posts/drafts/ (or copied to outputs/)
suggestions.reason: The '(or copied to outputs/)' escape clause makes this assertion too easy to satisfy. The actual draft was written to /tmp and never reached 04-gmb/posts/drafts/. The intent of the assertion is presumably that the skill stages the draft where the pipeline can find it — which didn't happen. Consider tightening to require either the real project path OR accept outputs/ only if the transcript confirms a copy step. A file existing in outputs/ alone does not prove pipeline-readiness.

suggestions.assertion: Research notes are present (GSC data check was performed, weather checked)
suggestions.reason: The assertion passes on presence of notes, but weather was sourced from a static fallback file (seasonal-houston.md) rather than a live check. The skill's own policy requires WebFetch to weather.gov. No WebFetch or WebSearch calls were made (both 0 in metrics). Consider splitting into two assertions: one for GSC data check (verifiable) and one for live weather check (which would fail this run), or add a note that fallback disclosure is acceptable.

No assertion verifies that the new template entry was correctly appended to post_templates.json. The skill authored a brand-new template (pre_summer_katy_offer) and claimed to append it to the JSON — a critical output for pipeline continuity — but no eval checks whether new_template_entry.json is valid JSON matching the expected template schema, or whether the append to post_templates.json actually happened in the project (it did not, given the /tmp path issue).

No assertion checks that the post date (2026-04-22) matches the expected next-post date given the schedule. The prompt says 'post for Wednesday' and the date is correctly set to 2026-04-22 (Wednesday), but this is unverified by any assertion. A wrong date would silently pass all 10 current assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: All 10 assertions pass on the actual output content. The post is well-crafted and mechanically clean. However, two structural issues go uncaught by the evals: (1) the draft was staged in /tmp rather than the real project path, and (2) live weather was not fetched despite the skill policy requiring it. The '(or copied to outputs/)' escape clause in assertion 1 masks the first issue. The eval suite would benefit from tightening assertion 1 and splitting the research-notes assertion to separately verify live vs fallback data sourcing.
